// diagnostic

E3410

`{module}.{call}` is a Tier-2 ambient comptime effect and can't run at compile time without a `#Impure` gate.

What

`{module}.{call}` is a Tier-2 ambient comptime effect and can't run at compile time without a `#Impure` gate.

Why

`core.files`, `core.sys`, `core.term`, and `core.process` touch the host system at compile time. Without the gate any build tooling (caches, hermetic sandboxes) may get different results.

Fix

wrap the call in `#Impure("reading config") { … }`.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E3410: tests/ui/comptime_io_rejected.stderr.

Error [E3410]: `core.files.read()` is a Tier-2 comptime effect — it requires a `#Impure` gate
  --> tests/ui/comptime_io_rejected.jet:4:13
    |
  4 | @data :: fs.read("config.txt")
    |             ^^^^
 Why: effectful Core APIs are not allowed in pure comptime evaluation
 Fix: wrap the comptime binding in `#Impure("reason") { … }` and pass `--gate impure=allow` to the build, or keep the call at runtime
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E3410

Error [E0107]: nothing named `@data` exists here
  --> tests/ui/comptime_io_rejected.jet:7:11
    |
  7 |     print(@data)
    |           ^^^^^
 Why: a name must be declared before it's used
 Fix: declare it first: `@data :: ...`
